funder_origin_name: Matsushita Electric Industrial Co., Ltd. (now Panasonic), with a personal gift from founder Konosuke Matsushita
funder_current_name: The Japan Prize Foundation, paying from the endowment donated by Matsushita Electric Industrial and Konosuke Matsushita
funding_share_basis: The 1983 endowment was entirely private: Matsushita Electric Industrial gave 10 million of its own shares (JPY 15.3bn) as a 65th-anniversary gift and Konosuke Matsushita added JPY 5.0bn personally (JPY 20.3bn total, ~75% corporate), and no other donor is recorded at founding; the Japanese government initiated the prize but put up no purse money. That same gift still pays the purse today. The Foundation's FY2025 statements (year to 31 Mar 2026) show endowment investment income of JPY 823.9m plus designated-asset income of JPY 95.6m against ordinary revenue of JPY 932.1m, versus only JPY 8.65m of donations received in the year (0.9% of revenue, 4% of the JPY 200m paid out as Japan Prize prize money). The endowment itself is JPY 30.87bn, of which JPY 30.04bn is the restricted donation corpus (指定正味財産 = 寄附金) and JPY 23.6bn is equities listed as 'Panasonic Corporation and 7 other issues'; the restricted corpus grew from JPY 22.8bn to JPY 30.0bn purely through valuation gains on those donated shares (基本財産評価損益等 +JPY 7.2bn), with no new endowment donations booked in FY2024 or FY2025. So more than half - effectively all - of today's purse is the original Matsushita money, not new money: funder_changed is false.
money_note: Each of the two annual field prizes carries JPY 100 million (JPY 200m total, booked as 日本国際賞賞金 in the accounts), doubled from the original JPY 50 million effective with the 2020 recipients; it is paid out of the Foundation's endowment investment income, not from current donations.
status_note: Prize name unchanged since 1985; the awarding body was renamed (Japan Prize Preparatory Foundation 1982, Science and Technology Foundation of Japan 1983, Japan Prize Foundation 2010). The 2020 and 2021 prizes were awarded on schedule but their ceremonies were postponed and held jointly with the 2022 ceremony on 13 April 2022 because of COVID-19.
judgment_reason: On funder_changed the evidence is unambiguous (endowment income pays the purse; annual donations are ~4% of it), but funder_current_type is arguable: the alternative is Corporate under the 'corporate-founded foundation' tie-breaker, since the endowment is still dominated by donated Panasonic stock and Panasonic alumni and Masayuki Matsushita sit on the board and asset-management committee. I chose Philanthropy because the Japan Prize Foundation is a legally independent Public Interest Incorporated Foundation (so designated Oct 2010) carrying no company identity, and Panasonic contributes no current money - the shares are a completed 1983 gift the Foundation is now selling down into bonds.
